Brains & Organisms Inside a Mathematical Universe

How physical/mathematical structure shapes life and mind — from thermodynamics and symmetry to neural manifolds and predictive brains.

Brains don’t float free — they are solutions shaped by geometry, entropy, and information constraints. “Order vs. disorder” is implemented as energy‑using inference machines that export entropy. Cognitive and cultural evolution exploit the same mathematics to build stable niches (for a while).

Physical Law & Symmetry (Geometry/Conservation)

  • Spacetime geometry constrains motion and signalling.
  • Symmetries ⇒ conserved quantities (Noether): energy, momentum, charge.
  • Limits: c (signal speed), quantum noise, Planck scales.

Thermo & Information (Order from Energy)

  • Brains are dissipative structures sustaining low entropy via energy flow.
  • Information has physical cost (Landauer); memory/erasure dissipates heat.
  • Shannon limits bound reliable communication.

Dynamical Systems & Control

  • Organisms are nonlinear control systems with feedback loops.
  • Brains exploit attractors & oscillations for robust function.
  • Predictive coding / free‑energy principle: infer causes, minimise surprise.

Neural Manifolds & Computation

  • High‑D neural activity often lies on low‑D manifolds (population dynamics).
  • Energy budgets constrain codes (sparse, efficient).
  • Levels of analysis: computational ↔ algorithmic ↔ implementational (Marr).

Scaling, Networks, & Cultural Niches

  • Allometric scaling (metabolism ↔ size) bounds brain/cognition.
  • Network architecture trades wiring cost vs. efficiency (small‑world, modularity).
  • Cultural/tech niches externalise memory & control (writing, code, AI).
